title: Semilocal completion normalization boundary system
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $x\in B$. For a finite set $\gamma\subseteq\operatorname{Max}B$, put $S_\gamma=B\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak m\in\gamma}\mathfrak m$, $B_\gamma=S_\gamma^{-1}B$, and $D_\gamma=\varprojlim_j B_\gamma/(x)^j$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For $\mathfrak n\in\gamma$, put $C=\varprojlim_j B_{\mathfrak n}/(x)^j$. The canonical localization map $B_\gamma\to B_{\mathfrak n}$ induces the coordinatewise principal completion map $D_\gamma\to C$ [def-trf-adic-ring-completion-map]. For a prime $\mathfrak s\subset C$, put $\mathfrak s_\gamma=\mathfrak s\cap D_\gamma$ and $E_\gamma=\overline{D_\gamma/\mathfrak s_\gamma}$, the integral closure in its own fraction field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The canonical map $B\to E_\gamma$ is the composite through $B_\gamma$, $D_\gamma$ and its quotient. Define $\Delta(x)=\{Q\cap B:\gamma\subseteq\operatorname{Max}B\text{ finite},\ \mathfrak n\in\gamma,\ Q\text{ prime minimal over }xE_\gamma\}$.

source.place: Theorem 5.3 (Rotthaus Hilfssatz), printed p.11, definitions of Γ(n), Bγ, completed localization maps, contracted primes, normalization and Δ(x).
